questions.stem: A card is drawn at random from a standard pack of 52 cards. What is the probability it is an ace?
questions.explanation: A is correct. 4 aces in 52 cards. P = 4/52 = 1/13. Option C (1/52) is the probability of a specific named card (e.g., ace of spades).

questions.stem: Two fair coins are tossed. What is the probability of getting at least one head?
questions.explanation: C is correct. P(no head) = P(TT) = 1/4. P(at least 1 head) = 1 − 1/4 = 3/4. Sample space: {HH, HT, TH, TT}; favourable: {HH, HT, TH} = 3.

questions.stem: Two dice are rolled simultaneously. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers is 7?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Favourable: (1,6),(2,5),(3,4),(4,3),(5,2),(6,1) = 6 outcomes. Total = 36. P = 6/36 = 1/6. Note: 7 has the highest probability of any sum on two dice — crucial SSC fact.

questions.stem: A bag contains 5 red, 3 blue and 2 green balls. A ball is drawn at random. Probability it is NOT blue?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Total = 10. P(blue) = 3/10. P(not blue) = 1 − 3/10 = 7/10.

questions.stem: A card is drawn from a pack of 52. What is P(King or Queen)?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Kings = 4, Queens = 4. These are mutually exclusive. P = 8/52 = 2/13. No overlap since a card cannot be both a king and a queen.

questions.stem: P(A) = 0.6, P(B) = 0.4 and P(A ∩ B) = 0.2. Find P(A ∪ B).
questions.explanation: C is correct. P(A∪B) = P(A)+P(B)−P(A∩B) = 0.6+0.4−0.2 = 0.8. This is the addition theorem of probability.

questions.stem: Three coins are tossed simultaneously. What is the probability of getting exactly 2 heads?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Total outcomes = 2³ = 8. Exactly 2 heads: HHT, HTH, THH = 3 outcomes. P = 3/8. Using combinations: ³C₂/2³ = 3/8.

questions.stem: From a group of 5 men and 4 women, 2 persons are selected at random. Find the probability that at least 1 woman is selected.
questions.explanation: B is correct. Total = ⁹C₂ = 36. No women (both men) = ⁵C₂ = 10. P(at least 1 woman) = (36−10)/36 = 26/36 = 13/18.

questions.stem: A box has 3 red, 4 white and 5 blue balls. Two balls are drawn without replacement. What is the probability both are blue?
questions.explanation: A is correct. P(both blue) = ⁵C₂/¹²C₂ = 10/66 = 5/33. ¹²C₂ = 12×11/2 = 66; ⁵C₂ = 5×4/2 = 10. The 25/144 distractor comes from incorrectly multiplying independent probabilities 5/12 × 5/12 (which is with-replacement logic).
